extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity, academics, university administrators, journalists covering scientific misconduct
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and observed practices for investigating alleged research data fabrication at universities, as illustrated by the Diederik Stapel case. Includes actions institutions took, features of a thorough inquiry, and reporting/communication practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate administrative action on allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspend the accused pending investigation when there are concerns of fabricated data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tilburg University suspended Diederik Stapel after concerns arose; immediate suspension is shown here as an institutional response to serious breaches of scientific integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an independent investigative committee chaired by a senior reputable scholar
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up a committee (preferably led by a respected, independent figure) to examine manuscripts and alleged misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rector of Tilburg set up a committee headed by W.J.M. Levelt, a former president of the Royal Dutch Academy of Sciences, to investigate Stapel’s manuscripts and report back by a set deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set a clear reporting deadline for the inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the investigating panel a target date to complete its review and report findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel was asked to report back by October — setting deadlines focuses the inquiry and communicates timeliness to stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate the specific works and document which publications are implicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which publications/manuscripts are under scrutiny and make that explicit in the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release did not specify which of Stapel’s many publications were implicated; this omission is presented as a shortcoming — a thorough investigation should state which works are examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughly review manuscripts and document how frauds were committed
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine publications in detail to determine if data were fabricated and document the mechanisms used to perpetrate fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim report documents in detail how the frauds were committed — this level of detail is recommended and can serve as a model for other institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify the scope and impact of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate and report how many papers, theses, or other outputs are affected by the misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim report identified at least 30 papers faked, 14 doctoral theses compromised, and around 150 publications under investigation — providing clear scope helps assess impact and remediation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine roles of students and collaborators and protect/exonerate the innocent
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate whether students and co-authors were complicit or victims, and explicitly state findings regarding their responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissions examined the role of his students and collaborators and concluded they were fully exonerated; explicitly addressing collaborators reduces collateral harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview and take whistleblowers seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to whistleblowers, document their reports, and avoid dismissing early warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report spoke to various whistleblowers and noted that initial whistleblowers were not listened to — ignoring early reports is an anti-pattern that investigations should avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the research environment and systemic contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Probe institutional culture and structures that may have enabled the misconduct or delayed detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissions looked at the research environment Stapel worked in and explored why it took so long to find the fraud, recommending institutional changes to reduce future risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate investigations across institutions when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When a researcher has affiliations at multiple institutions, coordinate inquiries and exchange materials among independent commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three universities that employed Stapel set up independent commissions but exchanged views and materials and produced a joint report — inter-institutional coordination can improve comprehensiveness and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make findings and recommendations public and detailed
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish interim/final reports that document findings, methods of fraud, and clear recommendations to prevent recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim report was made publicly available and described as a possible model for other institutions; transparent, detailed reporting builds trust and guides reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take remedial actions such as removing promotional materials or online endorsements
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or take offline publicity materials that present the accused as an expert while investigation is ongoing or where they are misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Tilburg website promoting Stapel was placed offline after the allegations — removing promotional content prevents misleading the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide opportunities for the accused to comment (journalistic standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempt to contact the accused for comment and include corrections when reporting errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes attempts to contact Stapel and includes a later correction about Levelt’s title — seeking comment and correcting errors are part of responsible reporting around misconduct cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use investigative reports as models and recommend reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce reports that not only document cases but also make clear, actionable recommendations for institutional reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The interim report made clear recommendations on measures universities could take to reduce the likelihood of such cases; such recommendations are a key deliverable of a good investigation.
